# Modules {.unnumbered}

The course is organized according to the five modules and contact-hour
allocations in the [syllabus](syllabus.qmd). Lecture materials are listed under
their syllabus module. Lecture numbering follows the course schedule; Lecture 00
was an introductory session and is not a syllabus lecture.

## 01 · Fundamentals of Probability and Random Signal Theory

**Allocation:** 9 lecture hours.

Probability spaces; conditional probability; independence; random variables;
discrete and continuous random variables; expectation; functions of random
variables; generating random variables; multivariate random variables; joint
distributions; functions of several random variables; joint moments; generating
multivariate random variables.

**01.1:** [Introduction to probability through problems · notes and materials](tutorials/01-probability-foundations.qmd).

**01.2:** [Random variables and distributions through problems](tutorials/02-random-variables.qmd): PMFs, PDFs, CDFs, joint, marginal and conditional distributions, with worked applications and independent exercises. [Advanced supplement](tutorials/02-random-variables-supplement.qmd).

**01.3:** [Worked tutorial: from outcomes to joint distributions](tutorials/02-joint-distributions-tutorial.qmd), with two interactive independence demonstrations.

**01.4:** [Worked example: two friends who may not meet](tutorials/04-meeting-problem.qmd), comparing two independent arrival models with an interactive waiting-time policy. [Fully worked appendix: actual waiting-time CDF, mixed distribution and moments](tutorials/04-meeting-problem.qmd#waiting-time-appendix), with CDF and density sliders.

**01.5:** [Expectation, mean and variance](tutorials/05-expectation-variance.qmd): discrete and continuous expectations, moments, covariance and conditional means. [Rigorous supplement](tutorials/05-expectation-supplement.qmd).

**01.6:** [Transformations of random variables](tutorials/06-transformations.qmd): CDF regions, auxiliary joint densities, Jacobians, sums, gaps and variable generation. [Rigorous supplement](tutorials/06-transformations-supplement.qmd).

**01.7:** [The multivariate normal distribution](tutorials/07-multivariate-normal.qmd): density, covariance, marginals, conditional laws, linear transformations and interactive two-dimensional demonstrations. [Rigorous supplement](tutorials/07-normal-supplement.qmd).

[Standalone proof: the central limit theorem](tutorials/08-central-limit-theorem-proof.qmd) develops the characteristic-function argument in full, including the finite-variance remainder estimate and the passage from transforms to CDFs.

These three lectures complete the planned Module 01 sequence. Their stopping points may span additional meetings as needed; the official syllabus allocation is unchanged.
